canonical_concepts.label: Virtual machine (VM)
definitions: A guest OS running on abstract hardware.

canonical_concepts.label: Guest OS1
definitions: A guest OS is de-privileged and no longer has full hardware access.

canonical_concepts.label: Hypervisor/VMM
definitions: Interface implemented by Hypervisor/VMM that runs on (usual) host OS, manages real hardware.

canonical_concepts.label: Virtual Hardware
definitions: Virtual hardware can have arbitrary features, largely independent of real hardware.

canonical_concepts.label: Virtual Machines (VMs)
definitions: isolated duplicates of the real machine

canonical_concepts.label: Containerization
definitions: Provides OS interface and executes software in a controlled way.
The main idea of containerization is to share the kernel among containers instead of having a separate OS per VM.

canonical_concepts.label: Container
definitions: process (set), created from image (image is template for container)

canonical_concepts.label: Virtualization
definitions: An old concept originating from IBM mainframes in the 1960s, aimed at better resource utilization and running different OS versions in parallel.
Creation of virtual/abstract version of something.

canonical_concepts.label: docker files
definitions: build recipes for images in simple text format

canonical_concepts.label: Hypervisor
definitions: A hypervisor or virtual machine manager (VMM) with full access to physical hardware.

canonical_concepts.label: Host
definitions: The environment in which the VMM runs.

canonical_concepts.label: Pod
definitions: group of containers sharing resources, unit of deployment
